question: According to Ramsar Convention, which of the following is World Wetlands Day?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd**____** February**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **World Wetlands Day** is an** environmental celebration **that began in 1971 when a group of environmentalists gathered to reaffirm the protection and love for wetlands, which are small ecosystems of plant life and organisms found within water bodies that provide abundant ecological health to not only water bodies but entire environments.
 
• The World Wetlands Secretary Department is based in** Gland, Switzerland**, and according to the Ramsar Convention, the first acknowledgment of World Wetlands Day was given to "the Iranian city of Ramsar on the Caspian Sea's banks."
 
• Every year on the second of February, **World Wetlands Day **is commemorated, but it was not established until **1997**.
 
• This day honours the good impact that wetlands have had on the world, as well as the importance of bringing people together for the benefit of Mother Nature.
 
• This day also increases global awareness about the importance of wetlands to people and the environment.
 
• On this day, community guardians and environmentalists join together to celebrate their love for nature via a festival that recognizes what wetlands have done for not only humans but all living things.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Ramsar Convention **on Internationally Significant Wetlands Waterfowl Habitat is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of wetlands, which is particularly important.
 
• It's also known as the Wetlands Convention. It takes its name from the Iranian city of Ramsar, where the treaty was signed in **1971**.
 
• Representatives of the contracting parties gather every three years at the Conference of the Contracting Parties (COP), the convention's policy-making organ, to adopt decisions (resolutions and recommendations) to administer the convention's activities and strengthen the parties' ability to achieve its goals.
